keyFindings.description: A decided block's body is outside every comparison: CutDecisionBlocks drops the whole ask node from both sides (:385) and carryVerdict skips a block whose row state equals the approved version's attributes (:293), so the question and options of an answered block are never compared. Settlement restores a decided ask's wording (ask_blocks.go:324-338) but only at settlement; the edits route (routes_table.go:154, authAny) refuses an edited ask only for readability (validateEditedAskBlocks, ask_blocks.go:419-427) - ASK_NOT_OPEN guards PATCH /asks alone (api/asks.go:399) - and writes its version in its own transaction before settlement (api/artifacts.go:893-908 -> NamedVersion/SnapshotVersion -> writeVersionTx -> carryApproval), which the branch's own TestAnAnswerCarriesWhenAnAgentEditInsideAnotherBlockLandsInItsVersion (api/approval_carry_test.go:433-450) shows carries a human's pending answer. So an agent that rewords an answered block's body through POST /edits inside the answer's settle window gets an approved review and artifact.approved in the approver's name over a version whose decided block shows his selected option under wording nobody decided; settlement restores the wording seconds later as a stale N+1. Combined with the Minor below (a deleted-then-restored answered block counts as newly answered) it needs no human action in the window at all. Bounded: text outside blocks still equals A, the answerer and answer text are row-backed, and the gate it can reopen is one the agent's own edit closed. Traced in code; not driven (no Postgres in this pane). Fix: for every ask node of N backed by a decided row (answered or resolved), require the node to ask the row's wording (block.asks(model.NewAskEditPrevious(ask)), the test settlement itself uses) and to show the row's state, else carry nothing; add the server test (approve with an answered block, answer another block, reword the answered block through the edits route in the window -> stale, one review).

newlyAnsweredBlocks decides the trigger against version N-1's stored attributes. Deleting an answered block leaves its row answered (only open asks are retracted, ask_blocks.go:390-397) and writes N-1 without it; re-inserting a block with that id makes the row back it again, so the block is absent from N-1 and answered in the rows, newlyAnsweredBlocks names the human, and the carry fires with no human action. The approved content equals A (the cut pins the text; settlement writes the decided wording back), so the record and the artifact.approved event are wrong, not the content. Option: ignore, as newly answered, a block whose row answer.at predates the approval being carried; or decide the changed set against A alone and require it non-empty. The architect may take it as a fast-follow if the Important's fix does not already cover it.

codeFenceEnd returns undefined for a backtick fence whose info string holds a backtick (correct per CommonMark: it opens no fence), after which the ask scanner reads the lines it encloses and cuts a :::ask block written inside them - the hidden direction. Reachable only from a live tree whose code_block language holds a backtick (the markdown parser refuses it, so the Go carry fails closed on such a version); consume that one line as text instead of letting the scanner see past it.
